name: Uzzah
bio: Uzzah was a son of Abinadab, one of the two brothers who drove the new cart carrying the ark of the covenant when David set out to bring it to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:3-4). When the oxen pulling the cart stumbled at Nachon's threshing floor, Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark to steady it — and the LORD struck him down on the spot for the act, so that he died there beside it (2 Samuel 6:6-7). David was both angry and afraid at the sudden death, naming the place Perez-uzzah ("outbreak against Uzzah") and, shaken, refused for a time to bring the ark any further into the city of David, leaving it instead in the house of Obed-edom (2 Samuel 6:8-10). The episode is traditionally read as a stark reminder that the ark was never meant to be transported on a cart at all, but carried on the shoulders of consecrated Levites by its poles (compare Numbers 4:15; 1 Chronicles 15:13), and that even a well-intentioned hand could not treat it as common.
